title: How many smartphones are sold in India each year? About 175M phones a year, estimated step by step
description: A step-by-step estimate for "How many smartphones are sold in India each year?" with the approach, the maths and a sanity check.
hook: Here is a step up to practise on. Read the question, pause, and have a go at your own estimate first, even a rough one. Then walk through the answer below and compare. Your number does not need to match; your logic is what counts.
body:
The question

How many smartphones are sold in India each year?

The approach

People × share with a smartphone ÷ years between replacements.

Say this out loud before you touch any numbers. It lets the interviewer agree with your plan, or nudge you, before you have done any work.

Step by step

  1. People in India: 1.4B
  2. × 50% own a smartphone
  3. ÷ 4 years before they replace it

That gives about 175M phones a year.

Does it make sense?

Close to half a million phones a day across the country, plausible for one of the largest phone markets.

This sanity check is the step most people skip, and one of the easiest ways to impress. It shows you care whether the number is right, not just whether the sum works.

Real-world check

Industry trackers put India at about 152 million smartphones shipped in 2025 (IDC). The estimate of 175 million is in the right range; a slightly longer replacement cycle, or a lower ownership share, would close the gap.

Source: IDC: India smartphone market 2025.

Your turn

outro: If your estimate was far off, look for which step made the difference. That is where the learning is, and it is exactly what an interviewer would ask about.
